# sv-grid

> The Svelte 5-native data grid. Headless engine + render component, AI-native, WAI-ARIA, virtualized to 100k rows.

Two npm packages: `@svgrid/grid` (MIT, open source) and `@svgrid/enterprise` (commercial - export, import, pivot, AI helpers).

For the full text of every doc page concatenated: see [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt).
For a machine-readable manifest: see [docs.json](/docs.json).

## SvGrid

### Overview

- [Changelog](https://svgrid.com/changelog): The user-facing log of what shipped. Format follows Keep a Changelog 1.1.0; versioning follows Semantic Versioning.
- [Getting Started with SvGrid](https://svgrid.com/getting-started-full): SvGrid is a modern, production-ready data grid for Svelte 5 - a headless core engine paired with a Svelte render component (<SvGrid>). It scales from a 10-row read-only table to a virtualized 100,0…
- [Getting started with SvGrid](https://svgrid.com/getting-started): SvGrid is a modern, production-ready data grid for Svelte 5 - a headless core engine paired with a Svelte render component (<SvGrid>). It scales from a 10-row read-only table to a virtualized 100,0…
- [Why headless?](https://svgrid.com/why-headless): SvGrid is **headless at the core**, with a fully-styled Svelte component shipped on top. That two-layer split is deliberate, and worth understanding before you reach for either.

### Getting started

- [1. Install](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/1-install): SvGrid is a single npm package. There is no peer dependency on a CSS framework - bring your own, or use the default theme that ships with the render component.
- [2. First grid in 60 seconds](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/2-first-grid): !Anatomy of the minimal example: a data rows array and a columns ColumnDef array flow into a SvGrid element that renders a small table with a header row and three body rows.
- [3. Data and columns](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/3-data-and-columns): SvGrid reads two arrays: data (your rows) and columns (the column-definition list). Everything else is opt-in.
- [4. Features](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/4-features): The grid engine is **feature-gated**. Out of the box you get the core row model (rows in their original order). To enable sorting, filtering, grouping, pagination, expansion, or selection, register…
- [5. Theme and density](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/5-theme-and-density): The render component (<SvGrid>) ships its own scoped styles. You re-theme it by declaring --sg-* CSS custom properties at any level above the grid - :root for the whole app, a wrapper <div> for one…
- [6. Going to production](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/6-going-to-production): You have a working grid. This page is the checklist that turns it into something you'd ship.
- [Starters & scaffolding](https://svgrid.com/getting-started/starters): The fastest way to a working SvGrid app. One command scaffolds a project with the grid already wired up - no copy-paste, no config archaeology.

### Cells

- [Cell components](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/cell-components): For any cell whose content is more than a string, use cell: with renderSnippet or renderComponent.
- [Cell data types](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/cell-data-types): The editorType field on a column tags the column with a type. This drives three different behaviours:
- [Cell text selection](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/cell-text-selection): By default the grid has **cell-range selection** (drag across cells, range highlight, copy as TSV). Standard browser text-selection inside a cell is **not** the default - clicking-and-dragging acro…
- [Conditional formatting](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/conditional-formatting): Conditional formatting colors a cell by its value. SvGrid ships it as a declarative engine prop, conditionalFormats, so you describe the rules once and the grid paints every cell - no per-cell cell…
- [Expressions](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/expressions): SvGrid does not ship a formula / expression language for cells. Computed values are JavaScript - either via fieldFn or inside a cell callback.
- [Getting values](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/getting-values): You get cell values in three ways depending on context.
- [Highlighting changes](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/highlighting-changes): Set cellFlash on a column and the grid flashes that cell whenever its value changes - edits, streaming feeds, server pushes. It is keyed by row identity, so scrolling a virtualized grid (which recy…
- [Sparklines](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/sparklines): A sparkline is a tiny, word-sized chart drawn inside a single cell. SvGrid renders them as a first-class column type: set sparkline on a column whose value is an array of numbers and the grid paint…
- [Styling cells](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/styling-cells): Cells render as <td> and pick up the same CSS variable tokens as the rest of the grid.
- [Text formatting](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/text-formatting): The format field on a column produces locale-aware formatted strings without you writing a renderer.
- [Tooltips](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/tooltips): There is no built-in tooltip API on ColumnDef. Use the standard title attribute, an accessible <dialog>, or any popover library - wired through a custom cell renderer.
- [View refresh](https://svgrid.com/help/cells/view-refresh): The grid renders reactively - it does **not** have a refresh() method, because it doesn't need one. To make the grid re-display, change the data that drives it.

### Columns

- [Aligned grids](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/aligned-grids): Aligned grids are two or more independent <SvGrid> instances kept in lockstep: **horizontal scroll** and **column-resize widths** propagate between them. Use it for a budget-vs-actuals comparison, …
- [Column definitions](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-definitions): A ColumnDef tells SvGrid how to read a value out of a row, how to render it, and which features apply to it. The grid below is built from a handful of ColumnDefs - look at the source to see how eac…
- [Column groups](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-groups): A column group is a ColumnDef whose columns array contains children. The parent renders a spanning header above its children. The pivot demo below shows three levels of grouped headers in action - …
- [Column headers - styling & height](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-headers): Headers are rendered as <th> inside a <thead> with role="row". Style them with regular CSS - there are no header-specific Svelte props.
- [Column menu](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-menu): Every column header carries a menu button (⋮). By default it's a flat list of actions plus a "Choose columns" submenu. Opt into the **tabbed** layout with columnMenuTabs:
- [Column moving (drag to reorder)](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-moving): There are two ways to move columns in sv-grid:
- [Column pinning](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-pinning): Pinning sticks a column to the **left** or **right** edge of the viewport so it does not scroll horizontally with the rest.
- [Column sizing](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-sizing): Each column has a pixel width. The default for all columns is the grid's columnWidth prop (default ~140 px); each column can override via its width field.
- [Column & row spanning (merged cells)](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-spanning): Spanning lets a single body cell cover **multiple columns** and/or **rows** - merged report headers, grouped labels, financial statements. SvGrid does this with a real colspan / rowspan merge engin…
- [Column state](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/column-state): "Column state" is the bag of per-column settings that change at runtime: visibility, width, pinning, sort, filter. SvGrid keeps these as separate state slices inside the grid instance.
- [Custom header components](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/custom-header-components): The header field on a ColumnDef accepts a function that returns either a renderSnippet(...) or renderComponent(...). The function receives a HeaderContext so it can access the column, header, and g…
- [Tool panel (Columns + Filters)](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/tool-panel): The tool panel is the docked sidebar - standard in enterprise grids - for managing columns and filters without hunting through a right-click menu. Turn it on with the toolPanel prop:
- [Updating column definitions](https://svgrid.com/help/columns/updating-definitions): There are two ways to change columns after the grid has mounted:

### Rows

- [Accessing rows](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/accessing-rows): You can read the grid's current rows in three ways.
- [Full-width rows](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/full-width-rows): "Full-width rows" are rows whose content takes the entire grid width instead of being cell-by-cell - useful for inline editors, banner ads, section dividers, and detail-row expansions.
- [Kanban board mode](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/kanban-board): Set one board prop and the grid renders its rows as **cards in horizontal lanes** instead of a table. It is the same <SvGrid>, the same data and columns - only the presentation changes. Lanes are b…
- [Master / detail (nested grids)](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/master-detail): Master/detail is the pattern where each **master** row expands to reveal a **detail** panel - most often a nested grid of the row's child records. SvGrid builds it from two props on <SvGrid>:
- [Row data](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-data): Row data is whatever you pass to <SvGrid data={...}>. It is a ReadonlyArray<TData> where TData is your row type. Any shape works; the grid does not require a base class or interface.
- [Row dragging](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-dragging): Managed row dragging lets users **reorder rows** within a grid and **move rows between grids**. Turn on rowDragManaged and every row becomes a drag source (grab cursor + a grip in the row-number ce…
- [Row height](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-height): Row height is a single integer in pixels.
- [Row pagination](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-pagination): Pagination is opt-in. Register the feature, register the row model, then either turn it on with showPagination or drive its state from outside.
- [Row pinning (top / bottom)](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-pinning): Pin specific rows to the **top** or **bottom** of the grid so they stay visible while the rest of the data scrolls. Typical use cases:
- [Row sorting](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-sorting): Sorting is a feature you opt into. Try it live - click any column header to cycle none → asc → desc → none; shift-click adds the column to the sort key list (multi-sort):
- [Row spanning](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/row-spanning): "Row spanning" lets one cell's content cover **multiple rows**, the way a merged cell does in a spreadsheet.
- [Scheduler / calendar mode](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/scheduler): Set one scheduler prop and the grid renders its rows as **events on a calendar** instead of a table. It is the same <SvGrid>, the same data and columns - only the presentation changes. Events are p…
- [Styling rows](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/styling-rows): Rows are <tr role="row"> elements inside the grid table. Style them with plain CSS.
- [Transactions](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/transactions): api.applyTransaction({ add, update, remove }) applies a batch of row mutations in a **single** data update - one re-render for the whole batch, not one per row. It's the path to use for high-freque…
- [Tree rows (expand / collapse)](https://svgrid.com/help/rows/tree-rows): SvGrid does not have a treeData prop. Tree-shaped data renders through the same data + columns pipeline as any other grid, with the tree behaviour living in *your* derived-state code. This is on pu…

### Editing

- [Edit components](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/edit-components): The grid ships with five inline editors. Each is selected by the column's editorType:
- [Full-row editing](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/full-row): Full-row editing opens an **entire row** for edit at once: every editable cell shows an inline editor, a single Enter (or clicking away) commits all of them in one update, and Esc cancels the whole…
- [Editing - overview](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/overview): Inline editing is a single prop on <SvGrid>. Try it - double-click any cell, type to replace, hit Enter to commit. Tab moves to the next editable cell:
- [Parsing values](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/parsing-values): When the user commits an edit, the editor's DOM value (a string for text / number / date inputs, a boolean for checkboxes) is parsed by parseEditorValue into the canonical value for the column's type.
- [Provided cell editors](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/provided-editors): The grid ships nine built-in editors, selected via editorType on the column definition. Each editor renders inside the cell while editing and falls back to the default text render (or your cell sni…
- [Saving values](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/saving-values): When the user commits an edit, the new value is written into the grid's **internal data copy**. The grid does **not** mutate the array you passed in via the data prop - it keeps its own working cop…
- [Start / stop editing](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/start-stop-editing): The cell must be **focused** (the grid's active cell). Click any cell or use the arrow keys to set focus.
- [Undo / redo](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/undo-redo): There is **no built-in undo/redo stack** inside <SvGrid>. The grid emits no per-edit event for an external stack to subscribe to, so undo/redo has to be built on top of the data-snapshot approach.
- [Validation](https://svgrid.com/help/editing/validation): There is no validate(value) callback on ColumnDef today. Validation happens by intercepting committed edits and either accepting or reverting them.

### Filtering

- [Applying filters](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/applying-filters): "Applying" a filter means running it against the data. SvGrid applies filters **eagerly** by default: every keystroke updates the row model and the visible rows (with a 150ms debounce inside the co…
- [Custom column filters](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/custom-column-filters): When the built-in operators and the set-filter pattern are not enough, take over the filter pipeline.
- [Date filter](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/date-filter): A column with editorType: 'date' (or 'datetime') gets the **date** filter operator set: equals, lessThan, greaterThan, **between**, isBlank.
- [Filter API](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/filter-api): Two surfaces - pick based on whether the caller is inside or outside the component that owns the grid state.
- [Filter conditions](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/filter-conditions): A "filter condition" is a (column, operator, value) triple. The grid stores filter conditions in state.columnFilters.
- [Floating filters](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/floating-filters): "Floating filters" are the always-visible filter inputs that sit **between** the header row and the body. In SvGrid the filter row is **per-operator and per-type**: each cell has a funnel to pick t…
- [Number filter](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/number-filter): A column with editorType: 'number' gets the **number** filter operator set: equals, notEquals, greaterThan, lessThan, **between**, in, notIn, isBlank, isNotBlank. The default operator is equals.
- [Filtering - overview](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/overview): Click any column header's filter icon to open the operator + value popover; numeric and date columns range-bucket their distinct values so the menu stays usable on big datasets:
- [Set filter](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/set-filter): A "set filter" (a.k.a. value filter, list filter) shows a checklist of all distinct values in a column and lets the user pick which to include. It's what you reach for to filter status to "active O…
- [Text filter](https://svgrid.com/help/filtering/text-filter): A column with no editorType (or editorType: 'text') gets the full **text** filter operator set. The default operator is contains.

- [Group aggregators](https://svgrid.com/help/grouping/aggregators): When grouping is active, each group row can show a rolled-up value per column - the sum of revenue, the average score, the count of deals. SvGrid does this declaratively: set aggregate on a column …

### Headless

- [Build a table from scratch](https://svgrid.com/help/headless/build-a-table): This is the whole point of headless: the engine computes the rows, **you** emit the markup. Here's a complete, sortable, filterable <table> in one Svelte component - no <SvGrid>, no grid CSS.
- [Controlled state](https://svgrid.com/help/headless/controlled-state): The engine never owns its state - **you do**. You pass state in and the engine calls your onXxxChange handlers with the next value. That one rule is what makes headless SvGrid click with Svelte 5 $…
- [Headless overview](https://svgrid.com/help/headless/overview): <SvGrid> is the **renderer**. createSvGrid is the **engine** that powers it. They're independent: you can use the engine on its own to build a custom UI, render a plain <table> for print or email, …
- [Row models](https://svgrid.com/help/headless/row-models): The engine turns your raw data into the rows you render by running it through a **pipeline** of row models. You opt into the steps you need; everything else is tree-shaken out.
- [Server-side data (load on demand)](https://svgrid.com/help/headless/server-side): When the rows live behind an API and there are too many to ship to the browser, the server does the work: **sorting**, **filtering**, and **paging** become query params, and it returns only the cur…
- [Styling a headless table](https://svgrid.com/help/headless/styling): With the headless engine you render your own markup, so **you own every pixel of styling** - there is no grid stylesheet to fight. The same createSvGrid engine can drive a minimal underlined table,…
- [Headless virtualization](https://svgrid.com/help/headless/virtualization): <SvGrid> virtualizes rows and columns for you. When you render your own markup, you virtualize yourself with the same engine SvGrid uses - createSvelteVirtualizer (reactive) or createVirtualizer (f…

- [Server filtering](https://svgrid.com/help/server/server-filtering): When the data lives on the server, the grid does not filter rows itself. It records what the user typed and emits a single **ServerFilterModel**, and your backend turns that model into a WHERE clau…
- [Server grouping](https://svgrid.com/help/server/server-grouping): Grouping a hundred thousand rows in the browser means shipping all hundred thousand rows first. Server grouping flips that: the backend runs the GROUP BY, and the grid receives **one pre-aggregated…
- [Server paging](https://svgrid.com/help/server/server-paging): When the Server-Side Row Model holds one page in memory, paging is just the act of choosing which page. The createServerDataSource controller turns a page index into an offset/limit request, asks y…
- [Server-Side Row Model (SSRM)](https://svgrid.com/help/server/server-row-model): When the data lives on the server - millions of rows in a database - the grid should hold only the page on screen and push sorting, filtering, and paging to the backend. SvGrid packages this as **o…
- [Server sorting](https://svgrid.com/help/server/server-sorting): In the Server-Side Row Model the grid never reorders the data - the server does, because only the server can see all the rows. The grid's job is to capture the user's intent as a sort model and han…
- [Server tree data (load on demand)](https://svgrid.com/help/server/server-tree-data): When a hierarchy is too large to ship up front - a file system, an org chart with tens of thousands of people, a geographic drill-down - you do not want to fetch every node before the grid renders.…

- [Date & time](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/date-time): Four date/time controls built on a shared, framework-free date engine (date-core, date-format, date-selection, date-restrict). They are the rich-by-default editors for date, datetime and time grid …
- [Feedback & display](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/feedback): Status, identity, loading and surface primitives for dashboards and detail panels. All are theme-token driven (light / dark + presets) and reduced-motion aware.
- [Headless editors](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/headless-editors): Every editor is **headless-first**, exactly like the grid (createSvGrid / <SvGrid>). Each Sv* component is a thin styled renderer over a framework-free runes core named create<Editor>. Import the c…
- [Internationalization & RTL](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/i18n-rtl): Every editor in the kit shares one localization + direction contract, so you wire it the same way everywhere.
- [SvGrid UI](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/index): **SvGrid UI** is the Svelte 5 component suite that ships in the free @svgrid/grid package - 70+ buttons, inputs, pickers, overlays, and layout primitives, each with its own tutorial page. Every one…
- [Inputs](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/inputs): Typed text controls. Each emits a clean value and themes from --sg-*.
- [Layout & composite](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/layout): Add any component with the CLI (drops a ready-to-edit starter into your app) - or add the whole family at once:
- [Navigation](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/navigation): Wayfinding components for admin apps and Studio-generated screens. Pure, keyboard-accessible, theme-token driven.
- [Overlays](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/overlays): App-chrome overlays built on the kit's shared accessibility primitives - createFocusTrap, lockScroll and createDismissableLayer - so focus, scroll locking and Escape / outside-click dismissal behav…
- [Range & feedback](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/range): Add any component with the CLI (drops a ready-to-edit starter into your app) - or add the whole family at once:
- [Selection](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/selection): List and overlay pickers. The overlay controls portal their panel to <body> (carrying theme tokens) so they never clip, and share a common option shape:
- [SvAccordion](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-accordion): A WAI-ARIA accordion of collapsible sections, with single- or multiple-expand and roving header focus.
- [SvAlert](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-alert): An inline, persistent contextual message - info, success, warning, danger, or neutral - with an icon, optional title, dismiss button, and trailing actions.
- [SvAutoComplete](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-auto-complete): A free-text input with a live-filtered suggestion list. Unlike SvComboBox, it accepts any value - the suggestions are just shortcuts - and it emits the raw text string.
- [SvAvatarGroup](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-avatar-group): Overlapping, stacked avatars with a "+N" overflow pill - the "assigned to" and "members" row for cards, tables, and detail panels.
- [SvAvatar](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-avatar): A user or entity avatar: an image with an automatic initials-and-color fallback, plus an optional presence status dot.
- [SvBadge](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-badge): A small status pill or count label - the quiet workhorse for statuses, counts, and tags across tables and cards.
- [SvBreadcrumb](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-breadcrumb): A navigation trail that shows where the current page sits in your app's hierarchy.
- [SvButtonGroup](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-button-group): A segmented button bar - a single-select view switcher, a multi-select toggle set, or a plain row of action buttons.
- [SvButton](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-button): The press primitive for the whole UI kit - a themeable button with variants, sizes, a built-in loading state, an icon slot, and automatic anchor rendering when you pass an href.
- [SvCalendar](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-calendar): A themeable, accessible month / year / decade calendar with every selection mode - the date surface the whole date/time family is built on.
- [SvCard](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-card): A themed surface container with an optional header, body, and footer - the building block for dashboards and Studio-generated app screens.
- [SvCarousel](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-carousel): A slideshow: a sliding track with prev/next arrows, dot indicators, optional autoplay that pauses on hover, and touch swipe.
- [SvCheckBox](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-check-box): A themed checkbox with a true indeterminate state and an optional inline label.
- [SvChip](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-chip): A compact, interactive pill for a selected value, filter token, or entity: an optional leading avatar or icon, a label, and an optional remove button.
- [SvCircularProgress](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-circular-progress): A circular ring progress indicator - determinate or spinning - with color intents, sizing and thickness, and an optional center label or custom center content.
- [SvCollapsible](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-collapsible): A single show/hide section: a header that toggles one region of content open and closed, with a smooth height animation. The standalone building block behind an accordion.
- [SvColorInput](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-color-input): A color swatch that opens a portalled popover with a hex field, the native picker, and a preset palette.
- [SvComboBox](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-combo-box): An editable combobox: type to filter a portalled option list and pick a value. Unlike an autocomplete, the value must come from the list - unmatched text reverts on blur. Filtering is local by defa…

- [SvContextMenu](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-context-menu): Wraps a region and opens a menu at the pointer on right-click or long-press.
- [SvCountryInput](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-country-input): A searchable country picker showing a flag, name, and dial code. It emits the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, so your model stores a stable 'US' / 'GB' rather than a display string.
- [SvDateRangeInput](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-date-range-input): A compact start/end field that opens a two-month range calendar with one-click presets (Today, Last 7 days, This month, ...). Emits an inclusive [start, end] tuple or null.

- [SvGauge](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-gauge): A radial arc gauge that renders a value within a range, with optional colored threshold bands, a needle, and a center label.
- [SvGridChart](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-grid-chart): An inline-SVG chart that renders a ChartSpec with no external charting dependency, built to bind to your grid's data.

- [SvRepeatButton](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-repeat-button): A button that keeps firing while you hold it down - after an initial delay, then at a steady interval.
- [SvResult](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-result): A full result page: a centred icon, title, description, and actions for the outcome of a flow - success, error, warning, info, or not-found. The whole-screen counterpart to a toast.

- [SvSegmented](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-segmented): A segmented control: a compact row of mutually-exclusive options in a shared track - the modern alternative to a small radio group or a tab strip for a setting.
- [SvSkeleton](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-skeleton): A shimmering loading placeholder that stands in for content while data is in flight - text lines, rectangles, and circles that echo the shape of what is coming.
- [SvSlider](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-slider): A single or dual-thumb range slider with steps, ticks, scale labels, and full keyboard plus pointer control.
- [SvSparkline](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-sparkline): A tiny inline chart - line, area, bar, or win/loss - drawn from a plain number array, with no chart library.
- [SvSpinner](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-spinner): An indeterminate spinner: a small spinning ring for "something is happening" when you cannot show real progress.
- [SvSplitter](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-splitter): Two resizable panes divided by a draggable WAI-ARIA separator, with pointer drag and arrow-key resize.
- [SvStat](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-stat): A KPI / metric card: a label, a big value, and an optional delta with an auto-colored up/down trend, plus slots for an icon and an inline chart.
- [SvStepper](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-stepper): A progress stepper for wizards and multi-step forms. It lays out completed, active, and upcoming steps so the user always knows where they are.
- [SvSwitchButton](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-switch-button): An on/off sliding switch with the ARIA switch role - the control for settings that take effect immediately.
- [SvTabs](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-tabs): A WAI-ARIA tabs widget with roving-tabindex arrow-key navigation, four tab positions, and optional closable tabs.
- [SvTagsInput](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-tags-input): An editable token / chips input - type to add, click x or Backspace to remove.

- [SvTextInput](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-text-input): The base single-line text editor for the whole kit - one control for text, email, url, tel, and search.
- [SvTimePicker](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-time-picker): An analog clock-dial time picker - 12- or 24-hour, minute snapping, and an hour-to-minute auto-switch. Drag the hand or click a number.
- [SvTimeline](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-timeline): A vertical activity or history feed: a connecting rail with a colored marker per entry, plus a title, timestamp, and description.
- [SvToaster](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-toaster): The host that renders the shared toast queue. Mount it once near your app root; call toast() from anywhere to push a notification.
- [SvToggleButton](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-toggle-button): A button with a sticky pressed on/off state, exposed to assistive tech via aria-pressed.
- [SvTooltip](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-tooltip): A small hover and focus tooltip anchored to its child, portalled to <body> so it is never clipped by a scroll container.
- [SvTour](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-tour): A guided product tour: it spotlights each target element in turn, anchors a popover with the step's copy, and walks the user through Back / Next / Done.
- [SvTreeSelect](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-tree-select): A single-select dropdown that shows an indented, collapsible tree in its panel - the cascader / tree-select pattern. Pick a node from a hierarchy, optionally showing its full path in the trigger.
- [SvTree](https://svgrid.com/help/ui-components/sv-tree): A WAI-ARIA tree view: expand/collapse, single-select highlight, cascading tri-state checkboxes, keyboard navigation, and - for large or remote data - fixed-row virtualization and lazy loading.

### Compliance

- [Audit log integration](https://svgrid.com/compliance/audit-log): A typed, tamper-evident audit trail of every user action in the grid, in under 50 lines. Pattern works for any backend - your existing audit table, Datadog logs, an immutable ledger (DynamoDB with …
- [GDPR + data residency](https://svgrid.com/compliance/gdpr): sv-grid is **GDPR-neutral**: the library never transmits personal data, never stores it server-side, and never logs it. If your app is GDPR-compliant before adding sv-grid, adding sv-grid does not …
- [HIPAA posture](https://svgrid.com/compliance/hipaa): sv-grid is **HIPAA-neutral**: the library does not transmit, store, or process PHI on its own. If your app is HIPAA-compliant before adding sv-grid, adding sv-grid does not break that compliance.
- [Compliance](https://svgrid.com/compliance/index): sv-grid is a client-side UI library - **all data stays in the browser**, the library never makes a network call of its own, no telemetry phones home. The compliance story is therefore short, but be…
- [SOC 2 posture](https://svgrid.com/compliance/soc2): sv-grid is a UI library, not a service - so it cannot itself hold a SOC 2 report. But it can sit inside a SOC 2-audited application, and the controls below describe the line where the library's res…
